required_fixes: Frozen decision rule short-circuits on F6 (degenerate discriminative power) before evaluating primary falsifiers F1-F4. F6 triggers on ANY arm with CI [1.0, 1.0], which includes both the treatment (A1) and construction-perfect baselines (A7/A8/A9). The rule order must be changed: F1-F4 should be evaluated before F6, or F6 should be restricted to null arms only.

Frame R (raw goal with identifier in request) is not a discriminating frame for the lexical-overlap null (A4). The prereg declared Frame B as supplementary and Frame R as primary, but Frame R cannot separate A1 from A4:shortest_first because the identifier appears in the goal string. The primary frame designation should be swapped or Frame R should be explicitly documented as non-discriminating for this comparison.

Induction cost discrepancy: prereg section 4.2 declares 150 requests for induction; section 4.3 defines 150/450 observations at 3 requests each (450/1350 requests). The executed code follows section 4.3. The frozen documents contain contradictory induction budgets. This is a measurement validity issue, not an infrastructure failure.

F8 (commit hash mismatch) is NOT_EVALUABLE because freeze.json records no code hash. This control-plane defect was already identified in EXP-GRAPH-36279237023. A code hash must be included in freeze.json for future experiments.
validity_findings: Measurement transaction completed validly: substrate contract all 5 checks passed (distinct cost multipliers, inheritance = 1 request, error rate 0.0, deterministic latency, correct verb transitions). 10,000 bind results, 10,000 execution results, 34,517 raw HTTP observations, 600 induction observations preserved. No infrastructure failure.

Split integrity maintained: training/test split by identifier families (read/update/delete) AND by collection; family-stratified bootstrap (B=5000) resamples identifiers within (family, collection) strata. No site/task identity leakage detected.

Representation integrity preserved: slot support inferred from observed path-segment value distributions across collections; no hardcoded vocabulary consulted during A1/A2 inference; raw path segments and state.collection preserved in mechanisms.json.
Confidence threshold frozen at 0.85 before any arm runs. ABSTAIN scored as distinct outcome class. Selective accuracy and coverage reported as pair.

Frame B is the only frame that discriminates the mechanisms. On Frame B, the lexical-overlap null (A4) scores 0.0 under both tie-break orders because the bare-ordinal goal contains no identifier token to overlap with. On Frame R, the goal string contains the full identifier, so A4:shortest_first achieves 1.0 bind accuracy trivially.

The experiment design's validity threat disclosure (prereg section 8.3) is accurate: single path template, synthetic identifiers, deterministic server, no LLM. These limit generalization but do not invalidate the mechanism-level question on this substrate.
Bootstrap procedure correctly implemented: family-stratified by (family, collection), B=5000, seed=42, unit of resampling = identifier. Intervals at 95% and 97.5% as preregistered.

A4 tie-break handling: both 'longest_first' and 'shortest_first' raw series preserved. Producer scores A4 at the better of two tie orders for F1 comparison (conservative for the treatment). This is explicitly documented and auditable.
baseline_findings: B-LEXICAL-OVERLAP (A4): Frame B bind accuracy 0.0 [0.0, 0.0] under both tie orders. Frame R bind accuracy 0.0 (longest_first) vs 1.0 (shortest_first). Semantic false-accept 1.0 on both frames. This null fails to reproduce the treatment on the discriminating frame.
B-POSITIONAL-REGEX (A5): Bind accuracy 0.0 [0.0, 0.0] on both frames. Semantic false-accept 0.0 (abstains 100% because pattern fails). This null is inert rather than wrong.
B-MOST-FREQUENT-VALUE (A6): Bind accuracy 0.0 [0.0, 0.0] on both frames. Semantic false-accept 1.0 (always binds most-frequent training value). This null fails completely.

B-DECLARED-VOCAB (A3): Bind accuracy 1.0 [1.0, 1.0] on both frames. Semantic false-accept 1.0 (transfers to 'products' and 'widgets' without discrimination). UNKNOWN precision undefined (never abstains). This is the incumbent string-matcher behavior.

B-COLD-RE-DERIVATION (A7), B-WITHIN-EPISODE-SCRATCHPAD (A8), B-RETRIEVAL-K5 (A9): All achieve bind accuracy 1.0 [1.0, 1.0] by construction (they re-derive or retrieve, not bind). Semantic false-accept 1.0. These are economic comparators, not binding nulls.
Positive control PC-MULTI-COLLECTION-VARIABILITY: A1 achieves bind_accuracy >= 0.95 (actual 1.0), executed_verified >= 0.90 (actual 1.0), semantic_false_accept <= 0.05 (actual 0.0). PASS.

Null control NC-SINGLE-COLLECTION-DECLARED: A2 on single-collection training shows variability degradation (bind_accuracy 0.34, unknown_precision 0.60 < 0.85 threshold). A3 on 'products' (out-of-support) shows semantic_false_accept >= 0.40 (actual 1.0) and transfer_rate >= 0.90 (actual 1.0). PASS.

F6_degenerate_discriminative_power.diagnosis: A1 hits ceiling [1.0, 1.0] because 100 in-support tasks from a single synthetic distribution yield no bootstrap variability. A7/A8/A9 hit ceiling by construction (re-derive/retrieve). F6 conflates clean separation with design ceiling effects.

cost_model_integrity.note: Induction budget discrepancy between prereg sections 4.2 and 4.3 disclosed but not an F7 deviation per F7 definition (per-task accounting)

claim_ceiling: The variability-learned binder (A1) demonstrates the mechanism-level pattern the Director mandate targeted: (1) it infers a closed-set collection vocabulary {items, orders, products} and head-to-prefix map from observed variability across 150 multi-collection training observations, with no hardcoded vocabulary; (2) it binds held-out in-support identifiers at ceiling (1.0) while abstaining on well-formed out-of-support 'widgets' identifiers (semantic false-accept 0.0, UNKNOWN precision 1.0); (3) single-collection training (A2) degrades to closed set {items} and correctly refuses 'products' (transfer 0.0); (4) declared-vocabulary incumbent (A3) transfers to 'products' and 'widgets' at 1.0 false-accept. The three structural nulls (lexical-overlap, positional/regex, most-frequent-value) all fail to reproduce A1 on the discriminating frame (Frame B). However, the frozen decision rule's F6 short-circuit prevents the frozen outcome from reaching SUPPORTS. The maximum justified claim ceiling is: C-PARAM-INHERIT mechanism-level behavior is CONSISTENT WITH a variability-learning mechanism and INCONSISTENT WITH the declared-vocabulary string matcher on the discriminating frame, but the frozen decision rule defect (F6 order) means the experiment's own frozen criteria return MEASUREMENT_INVALID. A repaired decision rule + re-run on the same raw evidence would yield SUPPORTS on Frame B.
unresolved: Whether the mechanism generalizes beyond single-template routes (/collection/id) to multi-template or real-Web path structures. The substrate is deliberately narrow per Scout validity assessment.

Whether the variability-learning approach transfers to cross-site settings (C-CROSSSITE claim) where collection names and path templates differ across sites. This experiment uses a single substrate with shared template.
Whether an LLM-in-the-loop agent (C-LLM-INHERIT) would exhibit the same mechanism/matcher distinction. This experiment tests the kernel mechanism in isolation.

The cost economics on this substrate show cross-episode induction dominated by within-episode baselines (break-even ~2,300-2,700 reuses). Whether this holds on real-Web substrates with higher re-derivation costs is untested.
The induction budget discrepancy (prereg 4.2 vs 4.3) should be resolved in the next freeze. The executed code followed section 4.3 (450/1350 requests).
